name: manual_8d06f9
claim: On shared coordination files, append and merge; never rewrite the whole file. A read immediately before writing does not make the write safe: two writers can read the same version and the second overwrite the first's addition, and a later re-read cannot recover text that no longer exists anywhere. Hold one shared lock across the read-modify-write, or use a compare-and-swap check (version, hash or modification time) that rejects a stale write, then re-read and re-apply; note what you superseded instead of deleting it.

decisions.notes: Supersedes the read-immediately-before-editing guidance with a lock or compare-and-swap requirement so concurrent writers cannot silently overwrite each other; the original record is preserved.
